mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced economic activity and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month indicates a strengthening labor market, which typically boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances when UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% in a single month signals increased demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances when HOUST increases by more than 5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a single month indicates a contraction in the supply side of the economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO decreases by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on mechanism where a high level of real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) relative to the previous month indicates strong consumer demand, which supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative more than 50% of the time when RSAFS is higher than the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a simultaneous increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3% in a single month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases & UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances when both PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.3% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and a decrease in consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.2% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy with controlled inflation, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate stable economic growth.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases & CPIAUCSL decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when both FEDFUNDS increases and CPIAUCSL decreases by more than 0.2% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional mechanism where a decline in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 0.5% in a quarter signals a contraction in the supply side of the economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, but only during a late-cycle contraction regime.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when GDPC1 decreases by more than 0.5% in a quarter during a late-cycle contraction regime.
